content:
Alex: Heads up — starting at ~11:42 we got a pager flood on the inference error-rate alert. Lots of identical 5xx/timeouts from quant beam workers. I was covering but Maya had to step away for a family emergency and won't be available for ~45m. There's a coverage gap.

Alex: Quick impact note: about 0.7% of requests are seeing timeouts but traffic is spiky; some customers with low TPS might see errors. Not a full outage, but noisy alerts are burning rotations.

incident-bot: Created incident INC-2026-451. Bridge: <https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-451>. Pager: Maya (primary) unavailable; Sam auto-escalated to secondary.

Sam: I'll take this. Checking logs now — looks like the quant kernel on a subset of nodes is throwing alignment errors across many requests (same stacktrace).

Jordan: Which alert id is triggering?

Alex: Alert is INF-9123 (inference-error-rate > 0.05 rolling 5m). Link: <https://redwood.monitoring/alerts/INF-9123>.

Alex: Proposing temporary suppress/noise-bump for 1h on INF-9123 while we triage — prevents pagers for already-acknowledged noise. Will follow the runbook. Thoughts? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Sam: +1 from me if we set an explicit snooze and post a note. We should also restart the affected quant-beam pool and failover traffic to non-quant variant for a small percentage to reduce customer impact. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pager-flood-response>.

Alex: Doing the ops command to snooze now:```
/ops alert update --id INF-9123 --snooze 3600 --note "Midday pager flood; noisy quant-beam nodes, snooze while triage"```

OpsBot: Alert INF-9123 snoozed for 3600s by Alex. Note: "Midday pager flood; noisy quant-beam nodes, snooze while triage".

Sam: Restarting quant-beam-pool-3 now (rolling). Will keep 10% traffic on non-quant model variant while we watch.

Liam: Rolling restart done on pool-3, tailing logs — initial errors drop off. CPU looks normal.

Sam: Monitoring metrics. Error-rate dropped from ~0.8% to 0.12% after restart and partial failover. I'm going to keep an eye for 10m.

Jordan: Good catch. Are we planning to change the alert threshold permanently or leave as snooze?

Alex: Temporary: snooze 1h. If stable for 30m, we revert to original threshold. I also created a follow-up ticket ENG-1245 for runtime team to investigate kernel selection/fallback (assigned to Maya).

Maya: I'm back now — thanks for handling this, team. I'll own ENG-1245 and start a deeper root-cause tomorrow. From what I skimmed, quant kernel mismatch between recent model compile artifacts might be the root.

Sam: Suggestion for next steps in the runbook: add an explicit grace-window step to avoid immediate pager storms when a primary goes offline but incident is being handled. We can formalize "snooze + notify" as a standard on-call move.

Alex: Agreed. I'll add a short note to the runbook and propose a config change to the alerting policy: allow a 5m > 3x noise suppression before escalating to page. Will draft an RFC.

Maya: Sounds good. I'll also include kernel artifact validation in the model onboarding checklist.

Sam: Closing loop: I'll un-snooze INF-9123 in 30m and watch. If it spikes above 0.02 (2%) sustained for 5m we re-open the bridge and page.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-451 marked resolved (stabilized) by Sam. Notes: snoozed alert, restarted pool-3, partial failover to non-quant, follow-up ENG-1245 created.

Alex: :white_check_mark: Thanks all. Leaving notes in the incident doc and adding postmortem tag for next-week on-call review."
